extracted.intended_audience: students and laboratory workers learning bacteriology/microbiological methods
extracted.subtask_description: Practical laboratory procedures and descriptive schemes for isolating bacteria in pure culture and for identifying and recording their cultural, microscopic, chemical, and biological characters. Includes methods of cultivation, working-up plates, descriptive terminology for colonies, microscopic/staining procedures, and biochemical tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of pure and mixed cultivations
rubrics_metrics.description: A cultivation which comprises the progeny of a single cell is termed a 'pure culture'; one which contains representatives of two or more species of bacteria is spoken of as an 'impure,' or 'mixed' 'cultivation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish whether cultivations are pure or mixed before further tests; isolation methods are required when mixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of isolation method
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of the method to be employed in any specific instance will depend upon a variety of circumstances, and often a combination of two or more will ensure a quicker and more reliable result than a rigid adherence to any one method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience is the only reliable guide, but as a general rule the use of either the first (surface plate) or the third (serial cultivation) method will be most convenient, affording opportunity for simultaneous isolation of several varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical separation — Surface plate cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolation by surface plate cultivation on solid media such as gelatine, agar, serum agar, blood agar, or by hanging-drop/block methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare plates as for nutrient gelatine/agar; use appropriate plate medium (e.g., wort for yeasts). Several plate types described with procedural steps for serum and blood agar preparation and inoculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical separation — Serial cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolation by serially transferring inoculum across a series of slanted tubes to obtain discrete colonies toward the end of the series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use at least four numbered slanted tubes; smear tube 1 thoroughly, then streak tube 2 without recharging loop, continue; discrete colonies usually appear in later tubes and can be transferred to fresh medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical separation — Hanging-drop or block culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Use hanging-drop or block techniques as a surface cultivation/isolation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced to other pages (see page 233) for technique; useful alternative to plate methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological differentiation — Differential media (selective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use media specially suitable for certain species which enable them to overgrow and choke out other varieties (e.g., wort for torulae and yeasts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example procedure: inoculate wort and incubate at 37°C 24 h, subculture repeatedly, then plate at 20°C to obtain yeast pure culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological differentiation — Differential media (deterrent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use media containing inhibitory substances that prevent growth of many species but allow particular species to grow (e.g., media with 1% carbolic acid inhibit most but Bacillus coli communis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose deterrent media to suppress unwanted organisms when isolating a resistant target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological differentiation — Differential incubation
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit differing optimum temperatures of species by incubating duplicate inocula at different temperatures to favor one species over another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: incubate at 40°C and 12°C to separate Bacillus typhosus (grows at 40°C) from Bacillus aquatilis sulcatus (grows at 12°C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological differentiation — Differential sterilisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit differing thermal death-points to kill one organism while preserving another (non-sporing) or to select for spores (sporing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-sporing example: heat to intermediate temperature between death-points (e.g., 58°C for ten minutes). Sporing example: heat at 80°C for 15–20 minutes to kill non-sporers and allow germination of spores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential sterilisation — Benzole bath apparatus and method
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a benzole bath construction (benzole between double walls boiling at 80°C) with inner water to maintain constant 80°C for differential sterilisation of sporing organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: place test-tube in water, ensure liquid level, wait until 80°C stabilizes, time 15 min, remove, then make cultures and incubate. Use pure benzole free from thiophene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological differentiation — Differential atmosphere cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt atmospheric conditions to separate aerobes from anaerobes or facultative anaerobes by incubating on solid media under appropriate atmospheric conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solid media for strict aerobes; for facultative vs strict anaerobes, perform rapid subcultures incubated aerobically to isolate facultative anaerobes, or use jars (Bulloch's or Novy's) with appropriate medium for strict anaerobes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological differentiation — Animal inoculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inoculate impure culture or original material into a susceptible animal to isolate certain pathogenic or strictly parasitic bacteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an animal specially susceptible to the organism; sometimes the only satisfactory method for sensitive organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working-up plates — Inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect plates carefully (without opening) with naked eye, watchmaker's lens, or inverted under microscope; mark distinctive colonies with grease pencil or choose nine haphazard colonies if differences are not apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark positions for later retrieval; use observation to select colonies for subculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working-up plates — Fishing colonies (stock dish method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer single colonies into a sterile Petri 'stock dish' divided into nine numbered squares; emulsify each colony in a small drop of sterile water for subsequent subculturing and microscopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number divisions to map colonies; prepare emulsions with sterile spatula and deposit on stock dish to create samples for Gram staining and subculture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working-up plates — Preliminary differentiation (Gram + morphology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare cover-slip film preparations from emulsions, stain by Gram's method, and examine under oil immersion to identify which emulsions represent different species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use results to decide which emulsions to subculture; repeat with additional stock dishes if some varieties are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working-up plates — Preparing isolation subcultures
rubrics_metrics.description: From selected emulsions inoculate agar slopes and broth tubes corresponding to each differentiation number, incubate, and identify organisms from subcultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store stock dishes in ice chest to await incubation results; if subcultures fail, re-obtain material from emulsions or re-moisten dried emulsions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme of study — Designation and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Record designation: originally isolated by (observer's name), date, and source of organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this scheme to ensure exact and systematic recording, especially for organisms not previously isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme of study — Cultural characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Study cultural characters on a range of media (gelatine plates, gelatine streak, stab, shake; agar plates, streak, stab; inspissated blood-serum; bouillon; litmus milk; potato; and special media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe at specified temperatures (20°C and 37°C where indicated) and include special media to demonstrate characteristic appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme of study — Morphology (microscopy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record vegetative forms: shape, size, motility, flagella, capsule, involution forms, pleomorphism; sporing forms and staining reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate microscopic methods (hanging drop for motility, stained preparations for structure) and measure individuals where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme of study — Chemical products of growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate chromogenesis, photogenesis, enzyme formation (proteolytic, diastatic, invertase), fermentation products (acid/alkali, indol, phenol), reducing/oxidising substances, gas formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform qualitative and quantitative assays as appropriate (e.g., estimate total acid production).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme of study — Biology (physical/environmental properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record atmosphere requirements, temperature preferences, reaction of nutrient media, resistance to lethal agents (desiccation, light, colours), chemical germicides, and vitality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test survival under different agents and conditions to characterise organism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme of study — Pathogenicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine susceptible animals (arranged in order), immune animals, experimental inoculation symptoms, post-mortem appearances; investigate virulence (length maintained, optimum medium, minimal lethal dose, exaltation/attenuation) and toxin formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange animal susceptibility data; measure virulence parameters and toxin production where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopic examination — General procedure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Make naked-eye and low-power observations of growth at intervals (e.g., every 24 h) using naked eye, hand lens, or 1-inch objective; distinguish superficial from deep colonies and note individual colony characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Chester's descriptive terms; measure diameter in mm at various ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopic description — Size
rubrics_metrics.description: Note diameter in millimetres at various ages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record measurements over time to capture growth dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopic description — Shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe colony outline: punctiform, round, elliptical, irregular, fusiform, cochleate, amoeboid, mycelioid, filamentous, floccose, rhizoid, conglomerate, toruloid, rosulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to figures for form examples when recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopic description — Surface elevation (general & detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record general elevation (flat, effused, raised, convex, pulvinate, capitate, umbilicate, conical, umbonate) and detailed surface texture (smooth, alveolate, punctate, bullate, vesicular, verrucose, squamose, echinate, papillate, rugose, corrugated, contoured, rimose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe under appropriate magnification to assess surface characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopic description — Internal structure of colony (microscopical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe internal microscopical structure: refraction weak/strong; amorphous, hyaline, homogeneous, homochromous; granulations or blotchings (finely granular, coarsely granular, grumose, moruloid, clouded); colony marking or striping (reticulate, areolate, gyrose, marmorated, rivulose, rimose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use microscopy to assess internal colony structure and markings; refer to figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopic description — Edges of colonies
rubrics_metrics.description: Record margin character: entire, undulate, repand, erose, lobate, lobulate, auriculate, lacerate, fimbriate, ciliate, tufted, filamentous, curled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine colony periphery carefully for diagnostic margin features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopic description — Optical characters & chromogenicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe optical attributes (transparent, vitreous, oleaginous, resinous, translucent, porcelaneous, opalescent, nacreous, sebaceous, butyrous, ceraceous, opaque, cretaceous, dull, glistening, fluorescent, iridescent) and pigment behaviour (pigment restricted to colonies, restricted to medium, present in both).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record colour and lustre and whether pigment diffuses into medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptions for streak/smear/inspissated blood-serum cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: For streak or smear cultures note similar points as for plate cultivations; in inspissated blood-serum note presence/absence of liquefaction (distinguish condensation water from liquefaction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use same descriptive vocabulary as for plate cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gelatine stab cultivations — surface growth, line of puncture, liquefaction character
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe surface growth as for colonies; line of puncture terms: filiform, nodose, beaded, papillate, echinate, villous, plumose, arborescent. Describe area of liquefaction (crateriform, saccate, infundibuliform, napiform, fusiform, stratiform) and character of liquefied gelatine (pellicle, uniformly turbid, granular, clear with flocculi, deposit at apex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use figures as reference for forms; record gas bubble production where present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shake cultures and fluid media descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: For shake cultures note presence/absence of liquefaction, gas bubbles, bulk of growth at surface (aerobic) or in depths (anaerobic). For fluid media note froth, pellicle, character of pellicle, body of liquid (uniform turbidity, flocculi, granules, clear with precipitate, colouration), and precipitate (character, amount, colour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully inspect both surface and body of fluids; record changes over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbohydrate media observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Note growth, reaction (acid/alkaline), gas formation, coagulation of serum albumen when serum water media used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record fermentation and gas production patterns for carbohydrate utilisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litmus milk cultivation descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: Record reaction (unaltered, acid, alkaline), odour, formation of gas, consistency (unmodified, peptonised, coagulated with clot character: hard/soft/ragged), whey (abundant/scanty; clear/turbid/coagulated by boiling or not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use table-like schema as given to record multiple aspects of litmus milk changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopical methods — Living preparations (motility and size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare hanging-drop preparations to determine motility or non-motility; observe at various ages and conditions since motility may be suppressed by unsuitable environment; measure size in non-motile or sluggish organisms with eyepiece micrometer or eikonometer and average results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not record an organism as non-motile from a single observation; perform series of observations under varying conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopical methods — Spore formation and germination (living)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe spore formation in hanging drops adding intravital stain (magenta 0.5%) if necessary; use 1/6
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select solitary bacillus and use immersion lens to observe spore formation; measure size changes with Ramsden micrometer. For germination, prepare hanging drops from old cultures or heat spores then transfer to broth and observe germination at intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopical methods — Fixed stained preparations for morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix cover-slip films and stain (Gram's method or dilute carbol-fuchsin), measure approximately 25 individuals with Ramsden's or stage micrometer and average; record pleomorphism noting predominant variant, medium, and period of development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixation example: exposure to 115°C for twenty minutes in hot-air oven; measure size accurately and report pleomorphism context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopical methods — Structure details (flagella, spores, involution forms, metachromatic granules)
rubrics_metrics.description: If present, record method of staining, position, arrangement and number of flagella; for spores record method of staining, shape, size, position within parent cell, condition of parent cell, optimum medium/temperature, age of cultivation, environmental conditions, and method of germination; for involution forms and metachromatic granules record staining method, character, shape, medium, age, environment, and for granules, number and colour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full contextual data for structural features to aid identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staining reactions — list and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Record staining results: Gram's method (positive/negative), Neisser's method (if granules noted record position and number), Ziehl-Neelsen's method (acid-fast or decolourised), and note which simple aniline dyes give best results (methylene-blue, fuchsin, gentian violet, thionine blue) with staining process details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note best dyes and exact staining procedures used for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biochemical methods — soluble products and metabolic tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Test cultivations for soluble enzymes (proteolytic, diastatic, invertase), organic acids (quantitatively and qualitatively for formic, acetic, propionic, butyric, lactic), ammonia, neutral volatile substances (ethyl alcohol, aldehyde, acetone), aromatic products (indol, phenol), soluble pigments, reducing power (colouring matters and nitrates to nitrites), and investigate gas production (H2S, CO2, H2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform both qualitative and quantitative assays appropriate to each product; record specific results.
